prompts.title: Christmas Family Photo by the Fireplace
prompts.prompt: Transform the uploaded photo into a warm Christmas family portrait. Keep every person's face, hairstyle and identity exactly the same. Place [the family] on a cozy sofa in front of a crackling fireplace with stockings, a tall decorated Christmas tree with warm fairy lights and wrapped gifts. Everyone wears matching [red knitted Christmas sweaters]. Soft golden light, shallow depth of field, shot on an 85mm lens, photorealistic, magazine quality, 4:5.
prompts.description: Turn any family photo into a cozy Christmas portrait with matching sweaters, a glowing tree and a crackling fireplace — faces stay the same.
tips: Upload one clear, well-lit photo where all faces are visible.
Say "keep faces exactly the same" — it is the most important line.
Change the sweater colour to match your family style.
For pets, add "and our dog sitting in front".

prompts.title: Snowy Christmas Market Couple Portrait
prompts.prompt: Create a romantic winter portrait of [a couple] walking hand in hand through a snowy Christmas market at night, keep the faces from the uploaded photo unchanged. Wooden stalls with glowing string lights, gentle falling snow, steam from mugs of hot chocolate, cozy wool coats and scarves in [burgundy and cream]. Cinematic bokeh, 50mm, natural skin texture, ultra realistic, 4:5 vertical.
prompts.description: A romantic night-time couple photo at a glowing Christmas market with falling snow and cinematic bokeh.
tips: Use a photo where both of you look at the camera.
Add "laughing" or "looking at each other" for a candid feel.
For Midjourney add your photo as an image prompt and use --cref.

prompts.title: Christmas Pet Portrait with Santa Hat
prompts.prompt: Turn my pet from the uploaded photo into an adorable Christmas portrait. Keep the exact breed, fur colour and markings. [My dog] wears a tiny red Santa hat and a knitted scarf, sitting next to a small decorated tree with presents and soft fairy lights. Warm studio lighting, sharp focus on the eyes, cute expression, professional pet photography, 4:5.
prompts.description: Your dog or cat in a tiny Santa hat next to a little Christmas tree — the cutest holiday card photo.
tips: Pick a photo where your pet's eyes are clearly visible.
Replace [My dog] with "My cat", "My rabbit" etc.
Ask for "reindeer antlers" instead of a Santa hat for a variation.

prompts.title: Personal Letter from Santa for Kids
prompts.prompt: Write a magical letter from Santa Claus to [child's name], who is [age] years old and lives in [city]. Mention that Santa saw how they [a good thing they did this year] and that the elves loved their wish for [gift]. Add one gentle encouragement for next year about [something to improve]. Make it warm, funny and full of North Pole details (reindeer names, the workshop, cookies). About 200 words, simple words a child can read, signed "Love, Santa".
prompts.description: Create a magical, personalised letter from Santa with your child’s name, age and good deeds — ready to print in seconds.
tips: Fill in real details — that is what makes kids believe.
Print it on parchment-style paper for extra magic.
Ask for "a version in rhymes" for younger children.

prompts.title: Christmas Card Messages for Anyone
prompts.prompt: Write 5 different Christmas card messages for [recipient: e.g. my boss / grandma / best friend / clients]. Tone: [warm / funny / professional]. Each message 2–4 sentences, mention [one personal detail], avoid clichés like "season's greetings". Then give one short version (max 12 words) that fits on a gift tag.
prompts.description: Five heartfelt, funny or professional Christmas card messages for family, friends, your boss or clients — plus a gift-tag version.
tips: Generate separate sets for family, friends and work.
Ask for a version without religious wording for clients.
Add an inside joke as the personal detail.

prompts.title: New Year Resolution Planner That Works

prompts.description: Turn vague resolutions into a realistic 12-month plan with milestones, weekly habits and a printable summary.
tips: Be honest about your free time — the plan adapts to it.
Ask it to "check in with me" monthly by saving the chat.
Add "make it fun" for gamified habits.

prompts.title: ATS-Friendly Resume Rewrite for Any Job
prompts.prompt:
You are an expert recruiter and resume writer. Rewrite my resume for the job below so it passes ATS filters and impresses a human reader.

Job title: [job title]
Job description: [paste the job ad]
My current resume: [paste your resume]

Rules: keep everything truthful, use strong action verbs, add measurable results where my resume hints at them, mirror the important keywords from the job ad, max 1 page, simple formatting (no tables or columns). After the resume, list the 5 keywords you added and 3 questions I should prepare for the interview.

tips: Paste the full job ad — keywords come from it.

Ask for a matching cover letter in a second message.
